html:
The Chickasaw Nation of Oklahoma is the government of the Chickasaw people in south-central Oklahoma, with its seat at Ada and its old capital at Tishomingo. The map draws its land in 1492, but the Chickasaw only came here in the 1830s. Their homeland, shown on the map as Chikashsha Yaki, lay in northern Mississippi and western Tennessee.

There they fought off Hernando de Soto in 1541 and later became allies of the British against the French. Under the Treaty of Pontotoc Creek of 1832 they gave up their homeland, and from 1837 they moved west to Indian Territory, one of the removals known as the Trail of Tears. At first they lived within the Choctaw Nation, then set up their own nation in 1856.

As one of the Five Civilized Tribes, they sided with the Confederacy in the Civil War, and their land was split into private plots before Oklahoma became a state in 1907. Today the Chickasaw Nation is one of the larger tribal governments in the United States. See also Chickasaw.
